sections.h2: What the Henderson County Clerk does for a seller
sections.html:
The clerk's land records office records and indexes the paper that moves title: deeds, land contracts, mortgages, liens, releases, plats and powers of attorney. It sits in the Henderson County Courthouse, 20 N Main Street, Suite 206, Henderson, KY 42420.

You can file three ways: bring documents in during office hours, mail them, or use an eRecording vendor. The vendors are Simplifile, CSC and ePN, and each charges the submitter its own fee. Wills, will disclaimers, state and federal tax liens and releases, and mobile home conversion affidavits can't go through eRecording, so file those another way.

After recording, originals come back by mail on the next business day, or you can collect them. Records reach back to 1786 and sit in record books, on microfilm, as digital images and online. A subscription service called TitleSearcher offers monthly or pay-as-you-go access to view and print recorded documents, handy when you need a copy of an old deed or release.

A standard deed costs $50 to record and a mortgage costs $80, under the fee schedule that took effect July 15, 2026. Each fee covers the first five pages, and each extra page is $3. Mortgages and a few other instruments include 30 pages.

Extra notations that reference another recorded instrument add $4 per reference. Plain copies sent by mail, email or fax run a flat $2 plus 50 cents a page, with a minimum charge of $2.50.

The rule in KRS 142.050 comes down to this: no tax, no recording. As grantor, the seller owes fifty cents on every $500 of value, rounded up for any leftover part, and the clerk takes payment at the counter.

On an ordinary sale, value is the full price, liens included. On a gift or token-price deed, it is the figure the open market would pay.

  • The tax is paid once per transaction, in the county where the deed must be recorded.
  • The clerk retains 5 percent and remits the rest to the county treasurer every quarter.
  • Foreclosure deeds, divorce transfers between spouses and deeds that merely correct an earlier one owe nothing.

sections.h2: What a deed needs before the clerk accepts it
sections.html:
Sellers get caught out by two requirements under KRS 382.135: a sworn statement of consideration and an in-care-of mailing address for tax bills.

The buyer and seller each sign the consideration certificate in front of a notary, either personally or through an agent. On a sale it confirms that the deed shows the full price. On a gift it says so and gives an estimated fair cash value. A swap states each property's fair cash value in the deed. When property passes at death, the personal representative files an affidavit before the estate closes.

The exceptions are few: utility easements, divorce-court transfers, rights of way for agencies, cemetery lots, same-party correction deeds and deeds to a local airport board. The airport deed skips the certificate but still owes transfer tax.

Land contracts follow their own rule. The contract names both parties, gives the buyer's mailing address, a legal description, the source of title and a preparation statement, and a notary witnesses both signatures. Transfer tax is collected when the deed follows, not on the contract.

The fee schedule covers a lot of local paperwork, and several items touch a sale or an estate.

  • Wills, $47 flat, and will disclaimers or renunciations, $46 each.
  • Affidavits of descent, $50, used when property passes by inheritance.
  • Plats up to 24 by 36 inches, $50, and their revocation, $50.
  • Fixture filings, $96, and fixture releases, which carry no fee.
  • Name changes, $46 flat, and articles of incorporation or organization, $46.
  • Marriage licenses, $60, and notary bonds, $19.

Military discharge papers are recorded at no charge. Certified copies run $5 with an extra 50 cents per page after the third.

Title searchers go through the clerk's encumbrance book. Here is what lives there, so you know what may need clearing before closing.

  • Lis pendens and judgment liens, $46 to record and $46 to release.
  • Federal tax liens, $46, and their releases, $46.
  • State tax liens and in-state child support liens, a flat $5 each.
  • Mechanic's liens, $46, plus a $60 charge to record a bond that releases one.
  • Assignments of a certificate of delinquency, $30, which come up when an investor buys an unpaid tax bill.

Every lien that turns up in a title search needs a recorded release. The payoff comes from you or from the closing proceeds, and the title company usually files the release afterward.

sections.h2: Unpaid property taxes and the clerk
sections.html:
The sheriff collects the bill first, then hands uncollected bills to the clerk, where interest of 1 percent per month plus penalties accrue until paid. A bill turns delinquent on January 1 following its due date.

You can settle a delinquent bill in person at the courthouse or mail a personal check, cashier's check, money order or certified check to Henderson County Clerk, 20 N Main Street, 2nd Floor Offices, Henderson, Kentucky 42420. Cards are accepted for a small extra fee. Call 270-827-5753 for details. At the tax sale, any qualified individual or company can buy the bill, and the buyer then has 50 days to notify the owner.

The buyer may sue to foreclose one year after the certificate is created. The property carries a lien until the bill is paid in full, so if you see an unpaid year in your file, clear it before a buyer's title company finds it.

Anyone who buys the bill must follow KRS 134.490, KRS 134.546 and the rest of Chapter 134. If you pay such a buyer, ask the clerk at Suite 206 for a copy of the recorded release for a small fee. Give it to the title company.

sections.h2: Getting ready to record a sale
sections.html:
Before closing day, check that the deed has the full price, the grantee's in-care-of tax mailing address and a notary on the consideration certificate. Ask the title company which vendor it will use for eRecording and whether you will need to bring any original pages to Suite 206.

If an old mortgage or lien shows up in the title search, a release has to be on record before the new deed can clear it. Releases carry their own fee, so ask the closer who will pay it. After recording, the original deed comes back by mail the next business day, and the buyer's copy follows the same route.

faqs.q: What is the recording fee for a deed in Henderson County, KY?
faqs.a: $50 for a standard deed, including the first five pages, under the fee schedule effective July 15, 2026. Each additional page is $3.

faqs.q: Can I record a Henderson County deed electronically?
faqs.a: Yes. The office accepts most documents through Simplifile, CSC or ePN. Wills, tax liens and mobile home conversion affidavits are excluded, and the vendors add their own fee.

faqs.q: Who pays the real estate transfer tax in Henderson County?
faqs.a: The grantor, meaning the seller. The tax is fifty cents per $500 of value, and the clerk collects it before recording the deed.

faqs.q: Do I need a notarized consideration certificate in Henderson County?
faqs.a: Yes, for nearly every deed. Both parties sign a sworn, notarized statement of the true consideration or, for a gift, the estimated fair cash value.

faqs.q: How soon do I get my recorded deed back?
faqs.a: Recorded documents are mailed back on the next business day, or you can pick up the original at the clerk's office.
